blocks.text: Chapter Forty-Four: Receiving the Prophecy of Bodhi

inline.s: If in times to come, even down to the very ending of the true Dharma, there are beings who have planted roots of goodness and have in ages past made offerings to countless Buddhas, then through the inspiring power of those Thus-Come Ones they shall obtain this vast Dharma gate, grasp and uphold it, and win the vast, all-knowing wisdom. In this Dharma they shall gain wide and deep understanding and be filled with great joy, and they shall preach it widely to others and ever delight in its practice.

All good men and good women who have sought, are now seeking, or shall seek this Dharma will all gain its benefit. You should abide in it without doubt, plant roots of goodness, and practice constantly, so that no doubt or hindrance remains and you do not fall into any kind of prison wrought from precious things.

Maitreya, beings of such great power and virtue can enter the manifold and vast gateways of the Buddha Dharma. But because they do not hear this Dharma, a hundred million bodhisattvas turn back from the unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.

If any beings copy this scripture, make offerings to it, uphold and read it, and for even a moment preach it to others, urging them to listen, without giving rise to grief or distress, and if they day and night contemplate that land and the Buddha's virtues, they will never turn back from the unexcelled Way.

At the moment of death, even if the three thousand great thousand worlds were filled with a great fire, such a person would pass beyond it and be born in that land. Such a one has already met the Buddhas of the past and received from them the prophecy of enlightenment, and is praised alike by all Thus-Come Ones. Therefore one should single-mindedly believe and accept it, and uphold, recite, preach, and practice it.

blocks.text: Chapter Forty-Five: This Scripture Alone Shall Remain

inline.s: Now, for the sake of all beings, I have spoken this Dharma of the scripture, that they may see Amitabha Buddha and his land and all that is there. Whatever should be done, you may seek it all. Do not, after my passing into extinction, give rise to doubt anew.

In the age to come, when the scriptural paths are extinguished, I, out of compassion and pity, will specially leave this scripture to remain for a hundred years. Those beings who encounter this scripture shall, according to their wishes, be delivered.

A Thus-Come One appearing in the world is hard to meet, hard to see. The scriptures and paths of the Buddhas are hard to obtain, hard to hear. To meet a good spiritual friend and, hearing the Dharma, to be able to practice it, this too is difficult. But to hear this scripture, believe it with joy, and uphold it, that is the hardest of all difficulties, and nothing surpasses this difficulty.

If there are beings who, hearing the name of the Buddha, are pure in heart and mind, leap with joy, the hairs of their body stand on end, or tears flow from their eyes, all this is because in their former lives they practiced the Buddha Way, and they are no ordinary people.

If people hear the name of the Buddha but harbor doubt in their hearts and place no trust at all in the words of the Buddha's scriptures, they have come from the evil paths; their past karmic misfortunes are not yet exhausted and they have not yet been delivered. Therefore their hearts are doubtful, and they do not turn toward faith.

blocks.text: Chapter Forty-Six: Practice Diligently and Hold Firmly

inline.s: The Buddha told Maitreya: The supreme Dharma of all Buddhas and Thus-Come Ones, the Dharma of the ten powers, the fearlessnesses, the unhindered and unattached, the profoundly deep Dharma, and the Dharma of the bodhisattvas such as the perfections, is not easily met. Those who can teach the Dharma are also rare in being able to proclaim it, and a time for firm, deep faith is hard to come by.

Now I have taught, in accordance with truth, this vast and wondrous Dharma gate, praised by all Buddhas. I entrust it to you to keep watch over it as a great protection, to benefit all beings throughout the long night of birth and death. Do not let sentient beings sink into the six realms and suffer all their dangers and miseries.

You should practice diligently, following my instruction. Be filial toward the Buddha and ever mindful of the teacher's grace. Let this Dharma remain long in the world without perishing. Hold to it firmly and never destroy or lose it. Do not falsify it, or add to or subtract from the scriptural Dharma.

If you think of it without ceasing, you will quickly attain the Way. My Dharma is thus, and thus I have spoken it. What the Thus-Come One practiced, you too should practice in accord. Plant and cultivate merit and goodness, and seek rebirth in the Land of Ultimate Bliss.

blocks.text: Chapter Forty-Seven: Merit and Wisdom First Hear It

inline.s: Then the World-Honored One spoke these verses:
Unless past merit, wisdom you sow, this true Dharma you cannot know; who served the Buddhas of the past believe, and their delight shall last.
Evil and pride, sloth, false view strand the Tathagata's subtle Dharma understand; like the blind who darkling stay, they cannot guide another's way.
Who planted good the Buddha's grace before, the world-saving deeds may now restore; having heard, they hold it, write it too, recite and praise, and offering do.
Thus with one mind they seek the Pure, in Sukhavati to be secure; though fire the triple world should roll, the Buddha's might shall them uphold.
The Tathagata's sea of wisdom deep, only Buddha with Buddha may keep; the hearers search through age on age, yet their utmost power can never gauge.
The Tathagata's virtue Buddhas know, the World-Honored One alone can show; rare is human life, rare a Buddha to meet, faith, wisdom, hearing, the hardest feat.
If beings are to reach the farther shore, their deeds past Samantabhadra's store; you who have learned and wisdom gain, should trust my teaching, it speaks in plain.
Blessed to hear this Dharma rare, call on the Buddha with joyful care; holding it, beings' stream they cross, the Buddha calls them friend, not lost.

blocks.text: Chapter Forty-Eight: The Benefits of Hearing This Sutra

inline.s: At that time, after the World-Honored One had spoken this Dharma, twelve thousand kotikoti of the beings in the worlds of gods and humans, freed from dust and defilement, obtained the pure Dharma-eye. Two koti of beings attained the fruit of the non-returner. Six thousand eight hundred monks, their outflows entirely exhausted, attained liberation of mind. Forty koti of bodhisattvas, abiding in non-retrogression from unexcelled bodhi, adorned themselves with the merit of their great vows. Twenty-five koti of beings attained the patience of non-retrogression. Forty thousand kotikoti hundred-thousand of beings, who had never before brought forth the aspiration for unexcelled bodhi, now for the first time brought it forth. Planting roots of goodness, they aspired to be born in the Land of Ultimate Bliss, to see Amitabha Buddha; and all of them shall be born in that Thus-Come One's land. In various other directions, one after another, they shall become Buddhas, all named the Thus-Come One of Wonderful Sound.

Moreover, in the Buddha-lands of the ten directions, both those already born there and those to be born in future times who see Amitabha Buddha, each direction has eighty thousand kotikoti of beings who receive the prophecy, attain the patience of the Dharma, and realize unexcelled bodhi. All those beings, through the karmic bond of Amitabha Buddha's past vows, shall all be born in the Land of Ultimate Bliss.

Then the three thousand great thousand worlds quaked in six ways, and manifold rare and miraculous transformations appeared; great rays of light shone forth, illumining the ten directions. Moreover, various heavenly beings in the sky made wonderful music and raised voices of rejoicing. Even the gods of the Form Realm all heard it and exclaimed at the unprecedented wonder. Countless wondrous flowers rained down in profusion.

Venerable Ananda, the Bodhisattva Maitreya, and the host of bodhisattvas and hearers, the gods, dragons, and the eight classes of beings, and the entire assembly, hearing what the Buddha had spoken, all rejoiced greatly, believed, accepted, and practiced it.
